entities.name: NADPH diflavin oxidoreductase 1
observations: The 768-residue query has a flavodoxin-like FMN-binding domain at positions 17–154, FAD-binding domains at 215–376, an NAD(P)-binding domain at 410–512, and a C-terminal RING-like zinc-finger region at 693–744.
Swiss-Prot homologs Q9UHB4, Q1JPJ0, and A2AI05 show 72.6–79.4% identity over approximately 70.2–70.7% of the query and are annotated as NADPH-dependent diflavin oxidoreductases.
The enzyme uses FAD and FMN to transfer electrons from NADPH to protein-bound [2Fe-2S] clusters in the cytosolic iron-sulfur assembly pathway.

The query annotation is supported primarily by strong homology and Pfam domain architecture; exact species-specific regulation and the C-terminal extension are not experimentally established for this sequence.

entities.name: NADPH reduction of protein [2Fe-2S]
observations: Candidate reaction: 2 oxidized [2Fe-2S]-protein + NADPH → 2 reduced [2Fe-2S]-protein + NADP+ + H+; mapped to Rhea RHEA:17327, RHEA:17328, and RHEA:67716.
The physiological electron acceptor is a protein-bound [2Fe-2S] cluster, especially in CIAPIN1 within the cytosolic iron-sulfur assembly machinery.

entities.name: FAD
observations: FAD is a prosthetic electron-transfer cofactor of NADPH-dependent diflavin oxidoreductase 1; ChEBI:CHEBI:57692.

entities.name: FMN
observations: FMN is a prosthetic electron-transfer cofactor of NADPH-dependent diflavin oxidoreductase 1; ChEBI:CHEBI:58210.

entities.name: Cytosolic iron-sulfur assembly
observations: The homologous reductase is a central electron donor in cytosolic Fe-S protein assembly, transferring reducing equivalents to CIAPIN1 and potentially CISD1.
